paper.title: EgoMem: Lifelong Memory Agent for Full-duplex Omnimodal Models

evidence.paraphrase: The paper presents dedicated retrieval benchmarks for face verification, speaker recognition and text-memory retrieval. It constructs 1,000 speaker-query utterances with 120 keys, a 5,000-pair speaker-verification test set, and 200 fact-retrieval queries against 500 candidate relation and personal-fact entries.

evidence.section: 5.2 Episodic Trigger Evaluation; 5.3 Personalized Dialog Evaluation
evidence.paraphrase: Held-out omnimodal token streams evaluate dialog-boundary memory with clean and noisy inputs, while personalized-dialog tests measure whether retrieved user profiles, facts and relations support fact-consistent responses. The paper states that part of the personalized omnimodal-dialog test set will be released.

adjudication_notes: Recorded separately from the EgoMem architecture per the corpus precedent for papers that introduce both a memory system and dedicated evaluation artifacts.
This is a collection of dedicated evaluation sets rather than a separately branded 'EgoMem-Bench'; the benchmark_name follows the manuscript Table 1 label.

The full-system evaluation is genuinely multimodal: face and voice identity are derived from raw audiovisual streams and route retrieval from persistent user memory, even though some sub-evaluations operate on text facts or public identity datasets.
